Propagating Tomato Trimmings In An Aquarium

Trimmed up my bigger Tomato plants today, removing the lower branches. These four were the best, and although they are not ideal for rooting, I think they should go. Waste not want not and all.

Here is one of the Tomato plants to be trimmed.

https://i.ibb.co/xmK3rr3/Mater-Blossoms.jpg

Step 1. Trim a branch off. I use a razor. After cutting them off the plant at a convenient angle, cut the bottom at a 45 degree angle to maximize vascular potential. Always slice by drawing your cutting edge across the stem and don't chop as it crushes the stem, even with a razor. Bypass shears will work as well, but I don't have those and a razor is simply best for this as you can do it with no crushing at all.

https://i.ibb.co/h1Z0RBx/Tomato-Trimmings-01.jpg

Step 2. Remove excess and/or yellow leaves. These cuttings were on the small side, so I just removed the worst leaves. If you are cutting from a large plant you may want to pare down the amount of leaves. Less leaves means the cutting has fewer to support as it tries to grow roots.

https://i.ibb.co/QQR4m5k/Tomato-Trimmings-02.jpg

Step 3. Make a float out of foam. This happens to be soft packing foam, about 1/2" thick. You want to put a slice in the foam to enable insertion and removal of the cutting after it roots. I also punched a hole. Since I had four cuttings, I decided to make the slices on each corner in a Windmill of Friendship pattern.

https://i.ibb.co/C1cfd5q/Tomato-Trimmings-03.jpg

Step 4. Insert the cuttings into the slots so that the stem will be in the water and the leaves will stay dry on top of the foam.

https://i.ibb.co/HV16qrn/Tomato-Trimmings-04.jpg

View showing the stem protruding through the foam on the underside.

https://i.ibb.co/RgWh0PM/Tomato-Trimmings-05.jpg

Step 5. Float your Mater Windmill of Friendship in a well lit aquarium. If you don't have an aquarium, you can use a bucket or something, just make sure you are not starting with chlorinated water and don't put it in direct hot sun. Aquarium water really is the best for rooting cuttings though.

https://i.ibb.co/zFppRm7/Tomato-Trimmings-06.jpg

In a week or so these should be rooting well enough to go into soil. This method works with most lush plants. Quick and easy way to multiply your plants.
